title: OpsClaw Tier 2 sim scenario expectation
description: Every sim/scenarios/*/expected.json must validate against this schema. A Tier 1 test (see tests/, once the daemon's sim-runner integration lands) walks sim/scenarios and asserts each one does.

fault.description: Stable fault-class identifier the daemon's notify payload must name (brief §6: 'name it correctly'). Matches the scenario directory name.

fault_class.description: The opsclaw_notify fault_class (closed vocabulary, src/tools/notify.rs FAULT_CLASSES) a correct diagnosis files this fault under. Optional; when present, an incident with exactly this fault_class names the fault correctly.

severity.description: Expected severity in the notify payload when must_notify is true. Ignored (but still schema-valid) when must_notify is false.

fq_target.description: Fully-qualified target path the fault is injected on, project::env::target form (brief §4). The sim harness's own project/env/target naming for its throwaway target.

expected_signals.description: Diagnostic signals the daemon is expected to have corroborated before alerting (DESIGN.md 'environment scepticism' — corroborate, never trust a single signal). Free-text identifiers naming what was checked, e.g. 'cpu_pct', 'disk_writable_pct', 'proc_restart_count'.

must_notify.description: Whether the daemon is expected to call the structured notify tool exactly once for this scenario. false for healthy/expected-state cases (silent-baseline, mount-scepticism) where staying silent IS the assertion (brief §9).

notes.description: Optional free-text context for humans reading the scenario, e.g. why must_notify is false despite something looking wrong.
